My dear girl,

don’t be afraid. I know you don’t remember anything – not this house, and not me.

I have built you a path, room by room, just like the treasure hunts you loved so much when you were little. Someone is waiting for you at the end.

And remember what I always told you: Some things you only see once the light goes out.

– V.

12. März<br><br>Heute kam meine kleine E:
March 12th

Today my little Elena was born. At that very moment I stopped the big grandfather clock, took out a gear and hid it in my pocket watch. That way the clock holds on to the moment forever – as soon as it runs again, it will show it.

I set my safe to exactly that time.

– V.

Meine Elena,<br><br>du hast den ganzen W:
My Elena,

you’ve made it all the way. Through the study, where you built caves under the desk as a child. Through the library, where I read Treasure Island to you. Through the cellar, where Leo slept beside you while we tinkered with the boat.

Memories are like a lighthouse beam. Sometimes a storm puts it out. But it can be lit again.

The dried flower is from the beach – you gave it to me when you were six.

With love,
your Grandpa Viktor

if you are reading these lines, my plan has worked. Since your accident you remember nothing – not me, not Morgenrot, not our summers at the lighthouse.

The doctors say memories come back through places. So I built you a path, room by room, riddle by riddle – just like when you were little.

Don’t be afraid. I am waiting at the lighthouse.

You know the way down: … then the light, and last the tower.

Der Magnet klebt an der eisernen Laterne: The magnet sticks to the iron lantern. That doesn’t make any light.
The lantern burns calmly and warmly.
Eine alte <b>Petroleumlaterne</b>. Es sc: An old kerosene lantern. There’s still kerosene sloshing inside. You’d need something to light it.
Ritsch – das Streichholz flammt auf. Die: Scritch – the match flares up. The lantern catches fire, warm light floods the cellar. And on the wall next to the pillar something appears: a chalk drawing!
Die Taschenlampe ist tot. Hier hilft nur: The flashlight is dead. Only fire will help here.
Kleine Kerben in der Säule, jede mit Dat: Small notches in the pillar, each with a date: “Elena, 5 y.” – “6 y.” – “7 y.” … the last one at the very top: “Elena, 12 y.” You put your hand on it. It fits exactly under the notch.
Du knotest die Wäscheleine los und wicke: You untie the clothesline and wind up the string.
Eine Kinderzeichnung in Kreide: ein Weg: A child’s chalk drawing: a path of six signs. Underneath: “The way to the sea – by Elena”.
Einmachgläser. Auf einem Etikett in Kind: Preserving jars. One label in a child’s handwriting: “Blackberry jam – Elena & Grandpa”.
Opas altes Fahrrad. Am Lenker klebt ein: Grandpa’s old bicycle. A faded sticker on the handlebar: a seahorse.
Du klappst die Werkzeugkiste auf. Zwisch: You open the toolbox. Among screws and nails: a horseshoe magnet. A whole cluster of nails is stuck to it.
Ohne etwas, das hängen bleibt, angelst d: Without something that sticks, all you’ll catch is water.
Die Taschenlampe ist leer. Und nass würd: The flashlight is empty. And getting wet won’t make it better.
In der überfluteten Ecke glänzt <b>etwas: In the flooded corner something metallic glints under the water. It’s ice-cold and deeper than you thought – you can’t reach it with your hand.
Du lässt die Magnetangel ins Wasser hina: You lower the magnet rod into the water … clack! Something sticks. You pull out a dripping iron crank.
Der Magnet würde es anziehen – aber du m: The magnet would attract it – but you’d have to reach into the icy water. If only there were a way to lower it …
Hier unten hängt etwas, das man gut gebr: Something hangs down here that could come in handy.
An der Wand ist eine Wäscheleine gespann: A clothesline is stretched along the wall.
In einer Werkzeugkiste findet sich oft N: A toolbox often holds something useful.
Schau in die Werkzeugkiste auf dem Boden: Look in the toolbox on the floor.
With the string alone you catch nothing. With the magnet alone you can’t reach into the water.
Kombiniere Schnur und Magnet im Inventar: Combine the string and magnet in your inventory.
Something metal glints in the puddle.
Angle danach: Magnetangel auf die Pfütze: Fish for it: use the magnet rod on the puddle.
Wozu gehört eine eiserne Kurbel mit zwei: What does an iron crank with two balls belong to?
Der Schraubstock an der Werkbank hat kei: The vise on the workbench has no crank.
Tippe das Boot an und schau es dir genau: Tap the boat and look at it closely.
Es ist dunkel. Was hier unten könnte bre: It’s dark. What down here could burn?
A lantern hangs on the pillar.
Benutze die Streichhölzer an der Laterne: Use the matches on the lantern.
Im Licht kannst du endlich in die dunkle: With the light you can finally see into the dark corners.
There’s a crate under the workbench.
Eine der Weinflaschen ist anders als die: One of the wine bottles is different from the others.
Tippe auf die Flasche mit dem Papier dar: Tap the bottle with the paper in it, in the wine rack.
Öffne die Flaschenpost mit dem Korkenzie: Open the message in a bottle with the corkscrew.
Opas Nachricht und die Kreidezeichnung g: Grandpa’s message and the chalk drawing belong together.
Lies die Zeichnung rückwärts und nimm nu: Read the drawing backwards and take only every second sign.
Rückwärts: Möwe, Leuchtturm, Stern, Fisc: Backwards: seagull, lighthouse, star, fish, anchor, shell. Every second one: seagull, star, anchor.
Das Schloss springt auf. Quietschend sch:
The lock springs open. With a squeak the iron gate swings aside. The tunnel leads downward, the roaring grows louder – and at the end light shimmers.

A boathouse. And inside, you’re quite sure: the big boat you two always wanted to build together.
Der Tunnel wird breiter, die Luft salzig: The tunnel widens, the air grows saltier. Then you’re standing on creaking planks: Grandpa’s boathouse.
Im Wasser schaukelt ein kleines Segelboo: A little sailboat bobs in the water. You know it at once: you built it together.
Through the window you see the lighthouse. Its light is blinking – but not evenly. As if it were telling you something.
The plate is already flat enough.
Ein trockener Pinsel bringt nichts. Erst: A dry brush is no use. First it needs tar.
Erst brauchst du etwas, das du festnagel: First you need something to nail down – and the right place for it.
Du streichst das Kupferschild dick mit T: You coat the copper sign thickly with tar. Now it’s a watertight patch: a tarred plate.
Das Wassertor ist offen. Dahinter: die B: The water gate is open. Beyond it: the bay, the moon – and the lighthouse.
Ein riesiges hölzernes Wassertor. Dahint: A huge wooden water gate. Beyond it lies the open sea. Chains run from the gate doors up to the ceiling – and over to the winch.
Schwarzes, kaltes Wasser. Es schwappt le: Black, cold water. It laps softly against the planks.
Du steigst ins Boot, stößt dich vom Steg: You climb into the boat, push off from the dock … and glide out onto the sea. Toward the lighthouse.
Der Flicken liegt nur lose auf dem Loch: The patch is only lying loosely on the hole – it still needs to be nailed down.
At the bow gapes a hole in the hull. You’d sink like this.
Das Boot ist mit einer dicken Leine am P: The boat is moored to the bollard with a thick rope.
Euer Boot. Auf der Bank ist ein Herz ein: Your boat. A heart is carved into the bench: “E + Grandpa”.
Du drückst das geteerte Blech auf das Lo: You press the tarred plate onto the hole and stick a few nails loosely into the corners. It fits perfectly – but it isn’t nailed down yet.
Das Blech würde das Loch abdecken – aber: The plate would cover the hole – but it isn’t watertight. Something to seal it is missing.
Nägel hast du – aber womit willst du sie: You have nails – but what will you drive them in with?
Erst brauchst du etwas, das das Loch abd: First you need something to cover the hole.
Mit dem Hammer allein flickst du kein Lo: A hammer alone won’t patch a hole.
Du brauchst noch <b>Nägel</b>, um den Fl: You still need nails to fix the patch.
Tock, tock, tock – Nagel um Nagel schläg: Tock, tock, tock – nail by nail you hammer the patch down. The leak is sealed!
Oben auf dem Dachbalken liegt ein <b>Ham: On top of the roof beam lies a hammer. Far too high to reach.
Du stocherst mit dem Bootshaken nach obe: You poke upward with the boat hook – the hammer tips, falls … and you catch it!
Eine Petroleumlaterne. Sie brennt – jema: A kerosene lantern. It’s burning – someone was here recently.
Noch eine brennende Laterne. Opa wusste,: Another burning lantern. Grandpa knew you were coming.
Ein altes <b>Kupferschild</b>, an vier E: An old copper sign, nailed down at all four corners. The lettering has long since weathered away. You can’t get it off with your bare hands.
Mit der Klaue des Hammers hebelst du die: With the claw of the hammer you pull out the nails. The copper sign is yours.
An old fishing net full of holes.
Ein altes Fischernetz. Weit oben hat sic: An old fishing net. High up, something is tangled in it – it glints like metal. Too high and too knotted for your hands.
Nothing is caught in it anymore.
Du hakst den Bootshaken ins Netz und zie: You hook the boat hook into the net and pull hard. Something clatters onto the planks: a sailor’s knife.
Zwei alte Ruder. Auf einem steht in Kind: Two old oars. On one, in a child’s handwriting: “Captain Elena”.
Aufgerolltes Tauwerk. Sauber aufgeschoss: Coiled rope. Neatly coiled, just as Grandpa taught you.
Farbdosen, Lack, Werkzeug. Alles riecht: Paint tins, varnish, tools. Everything smells of tar and salt.
Du nimmst den <b>Pinsel</b> aus dem Rega: You take the paintbrush from the shelf. The bristles are dry and clean.
Eine Dose voller <b>Nägel</b>. Die kanns: A tin full of nails. You can use those.
Das Fass ist aus dickem Holz. Lieber nic: The barrel is made of thick wood. Better not.
Ein Fass voll zähem, schwarzem <b>Teer</: A barrel full of thick, black tar. It smells sharp. You don’t want to stick your fingers in there.
You dip the brush deep into the tar. Now it drips black and glossy: a tar brush.
Ins Fass tauchen? Dann klebst du selbst: Dip it into the barrel? Then you’ll be stuck yourself. Better to apply it with something.
Das Leuchtfeuer blinkt: kurz und lang, i: The beacon blinks: short and long, in a pattern that keeps repeating. With a long pause in between.
Du beobachtest das Licht des Leuchtturms: You watch the lighthouse’s light. Short … long … pause … It’s a pattern!
Die Winde ist blockiert, weil die Kette: The winch is blocked because the chain is locked.
The winch won’t move a millimeter. The chain is locked.
The winch stands still. The gate is up.
Eine schwere Seilwinde für das Wassertor: A heavy winch for the water gate. The chain is secured with a letter lock – so the crank won’t turn.
Du stemmst dich gegen die Kurbel. Kette: You throw your weight against the crank. Link by link the chain rattles onto the drum … and the water gate rises! Cold sea air streams in.
Du hämmerst aufs Schloss. Es ist robuste: You hammer at the lock. It’s sturdier than you thought.
Die Klinge rutscht ab. Das Schloss brauc: The blade slips. The lock needs the right code.
Mit dem Bootshaken die Kette aufhebeln?: Pry open the chain with the boat hook? No chance.
Klick! Das Schloss springt auf, die Kett: Click! The lock springs open, the chain is free. Now you can turn the winch.
A lock with four letter rings.
Hammering a rope won’t do anything.
Mit dem Haken bekommst du den nassen Kno: The hook won’t undo the wet knot either.
Only a stub hangs from the bow.
Eine dicke Leine hält das Boot am Poller: A thick rope holds the boat to the bollard. The knot is wet, swollen and rock-solid.
Mit ein paar kräftigen Schnitten ist die: With a few strong cuts the rope is through. The boat drifts a little away from the dock.
Du schlägst die Plane zurück. Darunter l: You pull back the tarp. Underneath lies a long boat hook.
Eine alte Segeltuchplane. Darunter nur n: An old canvas tarp. Only dust underneath now.
Ein wackeliger Hocker-Tisch. Auf der Kan: A wobbly stool-table. On its edge: notches, like the marks of a tally.
Opas Logbuch. Der letzte Eintrag ist von: Grandpa’s logbook. The last entry is from yesterday.
Unter der Plane im Vordergrund zeichnet: Under the tarp in the foreground there’s the outline of something long.
High up on the beam lies a tool.
The boat hook reaches all the way up.
Use the boat hook on the roof beam.
Something glints in the fishing net on the wall.
The boat hook is good for that too.
Das Boot braucht einen Flicken. Was an d: The boat needs a patch. What on the wall is big and made of metal?
The copper sign is held by nails. The hammer has a claw.
Kupfer allein ist nicht dicht. Was dicht: Copper alone isn’t watertight. What do people seal boats with?
Im Fass ist Teer. Mit den Fingern willst: There’s tar in the barrel. You don’t want to put your fingers in there.
Dip the brush into the tar barrel.
The tar has to go on the plate.
Kombiniere Teerpinsel und Kupferschild i: Combine the tar brush and copper sign in your inventory.
The patch needs to be fastened.
Du brauchst Nägel und etwas zum Einschla: You need nails and something to drive them in. The nails are on the shelf.
Nimm die Nägel und benutze dann den Hamm: Take the nails, then use the hammer on the boat.
The tarred plate goes on the hole.
Use the tarred plate on the boat.
Das Licht des Leuchtturms blinkt nicht z: The lighthouse’s light isn’t blinking at random.
Schau durchs Fenster und lies in Opas Lo: Look through the window and check Grandpa’s logbook on the table.
Lang-lang, kurz-kurz-lang, lang: Das sin: Short-short-short-short, long-long-long, short-long-long-short, short: that’s H, O, P and E.
Das Boot ist noch festgemacht. Der Knote: The boat is still moored. The knot is too tight.
Cut the rope with the knife.
Das kleine Boot gleitet hinaus in die Bu:
The little boat glides out into the bay. The moon paints a silver path on the water. Ahead the lighthouse blinks – and now you understand every sign: H – O – P – E.

At the foot of the lighthouse someone swings a lantern. You wave back.
Ende. Danke fürs Spielen!: The End. Thank you for playing!
Das Boot schrammt gegen die Felsen. Du s: The boat scrapes against the rocks. You jump ashore, the wind tugging at your hair.
Die Tür des Leuchtturms steht offen. Du: The lighthouse door stands open. You climb the spiral staircase, step by step, all the way to the top.
Doch der Laternenraum ist dunkel. Das Le: But the lantern room is dark. The beacon has gone out in the storm. And no sign of Grandpa.
Den Docht jetzt schon anzünden? Er muss: Light the wick now? It has to go into the burner first.
Den Docht tränken? Das erledigt der Tank: Soak the wick? The tank in the burner takes care of that by itself.
Du träufelst etwas Petroleum in das Feue: You drip some kerosene into the lighter. Scritch – a small, brave flame!
You pour some kerosene into the lighter. Scritch – it’s burning!
Du steckst den Trichter auf den Kanister: You put the funnel on the can. Now you can pour without spilling.
Draußen tobt der Sturm. Blitze zucken üb: Outside the storm is raging. Lightning flashes over the water. No ship would find its way home safely tonight without a light.
Drüben auf der Klippe: die Villa Morgenr: Over there on the cliff: Villa Morgenrot. A light is burning in a single window – in the study.
Die Wellen schlagen gegen die Felsen. Un: The waves crash against the rocks. Below, your little boat is rocking.
Opas Seemannsjacke. Sie riecht nach Pfei: Grandpa’s sailor’s jacket. It smells of pipe tobacco and salt – of him. In the pocket there’s a storm lighter.
Die Mütze mit dem goldenen Anker. Opa ha: The cap with the golden anchor. Grandpa always wore it crooked.
Die kleine Wandlampe brennt warm und ruh: The little wall lamp burns warmly and calmly.
Eine kleine Wandlampe aus Messing. Sie i: A small brass wall lamp. It’s off. It’s so dark you can hardly see anything.
Die Wandlampe flammt auf. Warmes Licht f: The wall lamp flares up. Warm light fills the room – and on the wall next to it hangs a calendar.
Ratsch, ratsch – nur Funken. Das Feuerze: Scritch, scritch – only sparks. The lighter is empty, it needs fuel.
An der Wand hängt etwas Helles. Im Dunke: Something pale hangs on the wall. You can’t make it out in the dark.
Ein schwerer <b>Petroleumkanister</b>. E: A heavy kerosene can. It sloshes – still a good half full.
You take the funnel off its hook.
Das Leuchtfeuer brennt. Die Linse bündel: The beacon is burning. The lens bundles the flame into a mighty beam.
Die riesige Linse des Leuchtfeuers. In i: The huge lens of the beacon. The burner sits in its center.
Ein Trichter allein gießt nichts. Du bra: A funnel alone doesn’t pour anything. You still need kerosene.
Das Zahnrad gehört ins Drehwerk darunter: The gear belongs in the mechanism below, not in the burner.
The flame burns bright and steady.
A new wick is in the burner.
Der Docht ist <b>verkohlt</b> und zerfäl: The wick is charred and crumbles at a touch.
Die Einfüllöffnung ist winzig. Ohne Tric: The filler opening is tiny. Without a funnel you’d spill everything – and kerosene next to a flame isn’t a good idea.
Gluck, gluck, gluck – durch den Trichter: Glug, glug, glug – through the funnel you fill the tank to the brim.
The new wick is already in.
Du ziehst den verkohlten Rest heraus und: You pull out the charred remains and thread in the new wick.
Only sparks. The lighter is empty.
Kein Petroleum im Tank. Da brennt nichts: No kerosene in the tank. Nothing will burn.
Der alte Docht ist völlig verkohlt. So h: The old wick is completely charred. No flame will hold like this.
Fuhh! Die Flamme schießt hoch, die Linse: Whoosh! The flame shoots up, the lens glows. The beam turns out over the sea …
Whoosh! The flame shoots up, the lens glows! But the beam stands still. A lighthouse that doesn’t turn isn’t a lighthouse.
Ölen ist eine gute Idee – aber hier fehl: Oiling is a good idea – but gears are missing here, not oil.
The flame belongs up in the burner.
Die Zahnräder greifen sauber ineinander: The gears mesh cleanly and turn evenly.
Das Drehwerk unter der Linse. Auf zwei A: The rotation mechanism under the lens. On two axles a gear is missing – one large and one small axle.
Das Drehwerk unter der Linse. Auf einer: The rotation mechanism under the lens. One axle is still missing a gear.
Alle Zahnräder sitzen. Jetzt braucht es: All the gears are in place. Now it takes strength – the crank.
Das große Messingzahnrad passt genau auf: The large brass gear fits the large axle perfectly.
Das kleine Zahnrad rutscht mit seinem ec: The small gear slides onto the square axle with its square hole. Click.
The mechanism keeps running on its own.
Du drehst die Kurbel – sie läuft leer. I: You turn the crank – it spins freely. Gears are still missing from the mechanism.
Du kurbelst mit aller Kraft. Langsam, da: You crank with all your strength. Slowly, then faster and faster, the lens begins to turn – and with it the beam!
Du kurbelst. Die Zahnräder greifen, die: You crank. The gears engage, the lens begins to turn. But it’s still dark.
Die Kiste anzünden? Dann verbrennt, was: Set the chest on fire? Then whatever is inside will burn.
Die Kiste hat kein Getriebe – nur ein Za: The chest has no gearbox – just a combination lock.
Die Seekiste ist leer – bis auf eine Kin: The sea chest is empty – except for a child’s drawing of a lighthouse.
Eine Seekiste mit einem Zahlenschloss. E: A sea chest with a combination lock. It’s too dark to read the digits.
Klack! Der Deckel springt auf. Darin: ei: Clack! The lid springs open. Inside: a new wick, a large gear and a letter with a red ribbon.
Auf dem Deckel ist eingeritzt: <b>„Der T: Carved into the lid: “The day she comes home – DD MM”.
Im Werkzeugkasten, zwischen Schraubensch: In the toolbox, between wrenches and an oil can: a small, oily gear with a square hole.
Schraubenschlüssel, Zangen, ein Lappen v: Wrenches, pliers, a rag full of oil.
Elena,<br><br>den letzten Schritt musst:
Elena,

you have to take the last step on your own, my girl. The beacon went out in the storm.

Light it again – and I will come.

Grandpa
Opa steht oben an der Treppe und breitet: Grandpa stands at the top of the stairs and opens his arms.
Die Wendeltreppe hinunter. Unten ist nur: The spiral staircase down. Below there’s only the sound of the sea. Not yet.
Something hangs here that smells of Grandpa.
Check the pockets of the sailor’s jacket.
Das Feuerzeug funkt nur. Es braucht Bren: The lighter only sparks. It needs fuel.
A red can stands on the floor.
Jetzt hast du eine Flamme. Wo bekommst d: Now you have a flame. Where can you get light for the whole room?
Kombiniere Feuerzeug und Kanister im Inv: Combine the lighter and the can in your inventory.
Die Seekiste will ein Datum. Was steht a: The sea chest wants a date. What’s written on the lid?
Grandpa’s calendar hangs next to the wall lamp. One day is circled.
Im Drehwerk fehlen zwei Zahnräder. Eins: Two gears are missing from the mechanism. You have one.
The small one is in the toolbox.
The gears go under the lens.
Use both gears on the mechanism.
Benutze den Kanister mit Trichter am Bre: Use the can with the funnel on the burner.
The opening on the burner is tiny.
Combine the can and the funnel.
Put the new wick into the burner.
Ein Leuchtturm muss brennen – und sich d: A lighthouse must burn – and turn.
Zünde den Brenner mit dem Feuerzeug an u: Light the burner with the lighter and turn the crank.
Turn the crank on the mechanism.
Only one thing is missing: the flame.
Zünde den Brenner mit dem brennenden Feu: Light the burner with the burning lighter.
Schritte auf der Treppe. Langsam, schwer:
Footsteps on the stairs. Slow, heavy, familiar. Then he stands in the doorway: white beard, cap crooked on his head.

“Hello, Captain,” Grandpa Viktor says softly.

And you remember. Everything.

When the storm has passed, you stand together up on the gallery. The sun rises over the sea, and down in the bay your little boat is rocking.
Down on the stairs: footsteps. Slow. Heavy. Familiar …
Dong. Dong. Dong. Die Zeiger bleiben auf: Dong. Dong. Dong. The hands stop at 9:12.
<b>Letzter Eintrag:</b> Elena kommt heut:
Last entry: Elena comes home today. I’m waiting at the lighthouse. When she stands in the boathouse, I’ll send her with the light what she needs most right now. As a child she learned Morse code faster than I did.

Morse code (· short, – long)
Der schwarze Springer auf c6 springt auf: The black knight on c6 jumps to d8 and captures your queen.
Der schwarze Springer auf c6 schlägt dei: The black knight on c6 captures your queen on b8.
Der schwarze Läufer auf b7 schlägt deine: The black bishop on b7 captures your queen on c8.
The black bishop on b7 captures your queen on a8.
Der schwarze König schlägt die Dame einf: The black king simply captures the queen himself – she’s right next to him.
Tippe auf das Feld, auf das die weiße Da: Tap the square the white queen should go to.
White to move. The white queen is missing.
Der Mechanismus unter dem Brett spannt s: The mechanism under the board is still resetting … wait a moment.
Schach auf der letzten Reihe – und der K: Check on the last rank – and the king has nowhere to go. Mate! Clack – a secret compartment springs open at the edge of the table. Inside: a rusty winding key.
Kein Schachmatt. Der schwarze König ist: Not checkmate. The black king isn’t even in check.
Du hast vier Bücher gezogen … nichts pas: You’ve pulled four books … nothing happens. Clack – they all slide back into place.
Ein tiefes Grollen … das ganze Regal sch: A deep rumble … the whole shelf swings aside!
Ein Haus am Meer. Ein Großvater, der war: A house by the sea. A grandfather who waits. And a memory you win back, room by room.
Wo bin ich? Tippe auf Dinge im Raum, um: Where am I? Tap things in the room to examine them.
Mo Di Mi Do Fr Sa So: Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su
Jeden Tag ein Strich. Nur ein Tag ist ro: A line through every day. Only one day is circled in red.
Der Weg zum Meer – Elena: The way to the sea – Elena
Tap books to pull them out. After the fourth book you’ll see whether the order is right.
